objects.original: The pinned source includes f, W, an original minimizer, a regularized minimizer, and an algorithmic reduction.
objects.reconstructed: Continuous f, supplied global minimizer z, center x0, positive R and epsilon, actual W, constructed global minimizer w.
objects.evidence: The witness minimizes the displayed W itself; it is not a supplied minimizer of an unrelated function. Algorithm/oracle objects are absent, consistent with the three supported obligations.

domains.reconstructed: Whole proper normed additive commutative group.
domains.evidence: Euclidean spaces have compact closed balls. The module uses only continuity, compact-ball minimization and norm comparisons; no scalar structure or convexity is used. This valid broader domain still requires ProperSpace; complete infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces do not generally satisfy it.

quantifiers.original: The proof uses original and regularized minimizers and transfers the solver output accuracy.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every supplied global minimizer z, center and positive radius/accuracy satisfying the radius certificate, there exists one w satisfying both global minimality and radius comparison, followed by an implication for every x.
quantifiers.evidence: The same existential witness w appears throughout. The all-x implication is uniform, and does not provide an algorithm for finding x or expose w to an oracle algorithm.

assumptions.original: Convex beta-smooth Euclidean objective with an attained original minimum and initial radius certificate.
assumptions.reconstructed: Continuity, properness, global minimality of z, R>0, epsilon>0, and norm(z-x0)<=R.
assumptions.evidence: Source smoothness entails continuity and its Euclidean domain supplies properness. Convexity and beta-smoothness are unnecessary for the three comparison obligations. Positive R and epsilon make delta positive; the source small-accuracy regularization uses that regime. The omitted zero-radius and coarse-accuracy cases belong to the full algorithmic theorem.

conclusion.original: Full class reduction, including minimizer comparison and approximation transfer.
conclusion.reconstructed: Existence of an actual W-minimizer, sharp radius comparison, and epsilon/2-to-epsilon value transfer.
conclusion.evidence: The three conjuncts match exactly the supported regularized-minimum, radius-comparison and accuracy-transfer obligations. They establish neither curvature-smoothness nor oracle/class/query complexity. The changed curvature obligation label does not change the parent support list.

scopes.original: Global minimization and first-order algorithmic success.
scopes.reconstructed: Global minima and pointwise conditional value guarantee.
scopes.evidence: Minimizing over the compact radius-R ball is only the first step: the outside-ball proof upgrades w to a global minimizer using f(z)<=f(x). No uniqueness or convexity is asserted. The lesson correctly explains positive-coefficient cancellation and keeps first-order algorithm semantics separate.

constant_dependencies.original: delta=epsilon/R², two half-error terms, and radius at most the original radius; remaining smoothness and complexity parameters.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Same delta, exact radius comparison, and exact two half-error terms; no beta, phi or oracle bound.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The denominator is justified by R>0. Positivity of epsilon gives positive delta/2 for the radius cancellation. The constants are dimension-independent and contain no hidden factor. The small-accuracy comparison with beta is not needed for this parent component.

deltas.description: Only the explicitly bound proof component is admitted; full Lemma 4.2 remains incomplete.
deltas.evidence: No solver, class-uniform guarantee or oracle-cost theorem occurs in the displayed declaration. The publication binding accurately limits support.

deltas.description: The ambient domain is generalized within the displayed hypotheses.
deltas.evidence: Use Euclidean specialization for the cited paper. Do not compose the parent properness theorem on an arbitrary infinite-dimensional Hilbert domain.

deltas.description: Continuity replaces unused convexity and smoothness in the comparison component.
deltas.evidence: The compact-ball argument and outside-ball comparison justify the weaker assumptions. ProperSpace is available in the source Euclidean domain.
